gate: two-agent Chrome QA gate, plate wheel gesture matrix on engineering_2026-09-02_v7

environment.build: production, rebuilt and restarted by QA (pkill next-server; rm -rf .next/cache/images; npm run build && npm run start)
environment.browser: Playwright Chromium from ~/.claude/skills/gstack/node_modules/playwright, driven from bun
environment.why_not_browse: browse has no Input.* and no Emulation.* in its CDP allowlist, so real mouse, real touch and real reduced-motion emulation are not reachable through it
environment.rotation_read_from: --wheel-rot on .wheel-hub, cross-checked against the rendered matrix() of getComputedStyle(.wheel-hub).transform

input_fidelity.touch: real, Input.dispatchTouchEvent via page.touchscreen and a raw CDPSession
input_fidelity.hover: real mouse.move at raw coordinates, no actionability wait, wheel left turning

synthetic_or_weaker.method: Document.prototype.hidden overridden plus a dispatched visibilitychange
synthetic_or_weaker.why: Playwright pins every page to visibilityState visible; headed mode, ignoreDefaultArgs on the backgrounding flags, Page.setWebLifecycleState and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled all fail to hide it
no mouse gesture produces one and touch is excluded from the drag by design; the pointerup-outside-window and window-blur paths beside it were driven with real input

rows.row: ambient on arrival, after idle, hidden tab and back
mouse drag both directions, no click/dialog/nav/ghost, momentum then decay
slow press with no movement opens the menu
drag ending off-element, off-window, pointercancel, blur
hover pause and resume, tooltip, rapid sweep
Tab reaches each plate, tooltip, Enter, Escape, Tab away
trackpad scroll adds velocity and decays, no runaway
touch at 1024 and the phone row at 375
no leak, no console errors, no copy collision over a revolution
frame time and layout thrash during a drag and a throw

collision_sweep.method: 2D rectangle intersection, every on-screen plate image against the heading, all three About paragraphs and the Fresh always column, driven by real mouse drags

defects_found_and_fixed.title: the wheel stopped dead mid-throw and stayed stopped
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: onPointerLeave on the hub lifted the hover suspension, but during a throw the plates slide out from under a motionless pointer and fire pointerleave with no hand movement; the next plate then arrived under the same still pointer and the hover pause swallowed the throw
defects_found_and_fixed.repro: 1440x900, 250px throw released with the hand held still, 2 of 4 runs; never at 1280 (geometry and phase dependent)
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: only a real window pointermove (onIdleMove) lifts the hover suspension; the pointerleave listener is removed. A stuck suspension can only suppress the pause, never freeze the wheel, so the Lessons 25 hazard runs one way and this removes it

defects_found_and_fixed.title: a slow drag ended in a dead beat
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: a throwless release carried a released speed of zero and subtracted ambient from it, setting the wheel's speed to exactly nothing at the moment of release
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: a throwless release (stale hand, no velocity sample, or reduced motion) hands the wheel straight back to the ambient turn instead of decelerating it to a standstill first

defects_found_and_fixed.title: the keyboard focus ring landed below the fold
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: Chrome scrolls a newly focused element into view by the smallest amount that reveals it where it is, and does so after focusin; the wheel then eases that plate up to a full diameter away. Separately, Lenis owns the page scroll and a native scrollIntoView issued while Lenis has an animation in flight settles between the two

before.tab_from_page_top: top 1089 in a 900px viewport, scrollY 95, off screen

defects_found_and_fixed.fix: lib/scroller.ts publishes the Lenis instance from SmoothScroll so anything moving the page asks the scroll owner instead of racing it (native fallback under reduced motion, where Lenis never starts); the wheel centres the hub through it on a 500ms timer armed by a keyboard focus, after the browser's own scroll has landed. Gated on :focus-visible and bails while a pointer is down

recorded_not_fixed.title: a reverse throw passes through zero for 40 to 110 ms
recorded_not_fixed.detail: throwing the wheel against its ambient direction requires it to decelerate through a standstill before resuming forwards; measured 41 to 109 ms under 0.25 deg/s at the crossing over six runs
recorded_not_fixed.why_not_fixed: the dwell is set by AMBIENT / BOOST_DECAY_S = 2.143 / 0.45 = 4.76 deg/s squared; shortening it means shortening BOOST_DECAY_S, which would cut every forward throw short. Forward throws and parked releases both show zero flat frames, so the wheel is never left stopped

recorded_not_fixed.title: at 375, mid-scroll, the fixed Cosmos wordmark sits over the About paragraph text
recorded_not_fixed.detail: visible in docs/handoffs/screens/qa_2026-09-02_v4/mobile-row-375.png; Lesson 17's drop shadow is doing some work but the overlap is legible-ish rather than clean

behaviour_confirmed_as_designed_not_a_bu: closing the menu with the Escape key returns focus to the plate with :focus-visible, and the wheel then holds still until focus moves; this is the focus pause, not a stuck wheel
a 1400ms long press on a touchscreen opens the menu, which is the distance-only click rule James set, applied consistently
a 5927px scroll flick turns the wheel only about 3 degrees because the band leaves the viewport and the IntersectionObserver stops the loop
184 of 286 frames in a rapid hover sweep show two pills above zero opacity, which is the 80ms cross-fade between plates; at 40ms only one is at full opacity
not_tested: a real browser tab switch (Playwright pins pages visible; the handler and its document.hidden read were exercised, the browser's own switch was not)
a real pointercancel (dispatched synthetically; no mouse gesture produces one and touch is excluded from the drag by design)
real hardware: a physical mouse, a physical trackpad, a physical touchscreen
the OS-level reduced-motion setting (the media query was emulated at the browser level)
